source.title: Rapid Vapor-Driven Plasma Contamination and Suppressed Net Lithium Surface Loss in the HIDRA Stellarator

observed_or_inferred.effective_net_loss_suppression_factor: approximately 0.91 to unity in reported HIDRA hydrogen/helium cases
observed_or_inferred.plasma_behavior: high-temperature lithium release rapidly made the plasma lithium-dominated; stable vapor-shielding-relevant operation was not sustained
observed_or_inferred.qualification: R_eff is an effective model-referenced mass-balance estimate absorbing redeposition/recycling and possible surface-conditioning effects

limitations: HIDRA modeled heat fluxes in this campaign were orders of magnitude below reactor-relevant divertor conditions
initial Li inventory uncertainty estimated at roughly 15 percent
not a reactor-level availability, net-electricity, or cost measurement
project_effect: Add gross evaporation, net loss, redeposition, plasma impurity, capture/recovery, stability, cleanup, downtime and component lifetime as distinct FUS-001 variables; propagate only after independent replication.

lanes.D: plasma-facing material and diagnostic process windows remain open
lanes.H: dated literature watch and strategic integration

next_gate: Pin source/supplementary data, reconstruct uncertainty, preregister matched capture/control test, independently replicate and propagate to net delivered electricity.
